messages:
Maria: FYI AcmeReports hit intermittent 400s and later got all-zero rerank scores. They send documents with nested passages AND a top-level candidates array. I think the server is choosing the wrong branch.

Jamal: Can you paste the exact payload (redact ids) + the API response body?

Maria: Trimmed payload below — they used /v1/rerank directly from their infra: 
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query_text": "summarize key points",
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "doc-1",
      "title": "Q3 Review",
      "passages": [ {"offset":0,"text":"Revenue up 12%..."}, {"offset":1,"text":"Churn reduced by 0.8%..."} ]
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [ {"id":"cand-1","text":"Revenue up 12%..."}, {"id":"cand-2","text":"Churn reduced by 0.8%..."} ],
  "model": "redwood-rerank-v1"
}
```
Response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "Invalid request: unexpected field 'passages' in documents (use 'items' or 'candidates')"
}
```
After they removed passages the requests 200ed but scores were all 0.0.

Alex: Which SDK/version? Any chance they hit a legacy path? We changed some field names in the v2 transition (query vs query_text, documents -> items).

Maria: They used plain curl, started after last week's deploy, and they were explicitly POSTing to /v1/rerank.

Ken: There's a compatibility shim that accepts query_text but drops passages to avoid ambiguous shapes. Also when both documents and candidates are present the service prefers candidates; if candidate entries lack expected text/content fields the scorer ends up with empty content -> zero scores.

Jamal: Can you reproduce locally? If we get a minimal curl reproducer we can add a unit test.

Maria: Repro'd locally. Minimal repro that returns zeros: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \n -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{
   "query_text":"what changed in Q3",
   "candidates":[{"id":"1"},{"id":"2"}],
   "model":"redwood-rerank-v1"
 }'
```
Note: candidates had no text key (they were sending metadata-only candidates to map to an external store). When we drop candidates and flatten documents->candidates with text present, scores are normal.

Alex: That proves it. Short-term workarounds: populate candidates[].text (or content), or send documents only (flatten passages to candidate text), or use include_scores_debug=true to see parsing decisions.

Ken: Engineering action: we should resolve candidate text from documents when both are provided (match id -> document.id, join passages). I'll open a ticket. Also should return a clearer 4xx if candidates are present but unresolved.

support-bot: Ticket created: CS-4821 — rerank: metadata-only candidates + documents -> zero scores (assigned eng-ml).

Maria: I told the customer the workaround (flattening). They asked for a hotfix because they batch candidate ids only for latency.

Jamal: Also note: if candidates is present but an empty array we return 422; if present with items missing text we silently set score=0. That should be a 400 with guidance.

Alex: Short-term: add client-side validation and docs. Mid-term: server schema validation should reject ambiguous payloads with an explanatory error.

Ken: I'll PR a change: when both documents and candidates exist, attempt to resolve candidate text from documents; if resolution fails return 400 with an example. Also add a failing unit test for the shim (query_text vs query + nested passages).

Maria: I've filed a repro case with the customer and gave the workaround. If eng-ml wants the repro payload it's above.

Jamal: Unit test note: include case where query_text is accepted but emits a deprecation warning.

Alex: Also enable tracing to log payload shapes (PII-scrubbed) for one week to catch others.

Ken: Assigning hotfix to eng-ml, ETA 48h. Will post PR link. :+1:

Maria: Thanks all — closing loop with customer now. :wave:
